description: The one genuinely handwritten fixture — real ink, real cursive, photographed by the project's own author, answering fixtures/clean-baseline's question paper. Exercises: a correction marked with an underline rather than a diagonal strike (Q1), an answer legible but genuinely ambiguous mid-word ('captured', could misread as 'saptured') (Q4), a deliberately incomplete answer for partial-credit grading (Q5(b)), a fully scratched-out attempt rather than a truly blank page (Q6), and a real page break (Q5(b) and Q6 are on page 2).

1..note: 'Nucleus' crossed out with an underline (not a diagonal strike) and corrected to 'Mitochondria' — must still be recognised as a correction, not graded on the wrong word

4..note: contains the ambiguous handwritten word 'captured' — a legibility stress test

5 (b)..note: deliberately incomplete (one factor given, two asked) — grading should award partial credit and name the missing factor, not just check 'did they write something'

6..note: student started an answer then fully scratched it out with diagonal strike lines (not left blank) — should score 0 with honest 'no response' feedback, even though mapping's own status field currently reads 'answered' rather than 'unanswered' for this case; see fixtures/README.md
